prompt: I have 18 hours of work due this week, only 10 focused hours available, and I keep trying to fit everything in. Help me make a plan.
expected: Names overcommitment, compares load with capacity, requires a specific cut or renegotiation, and gives an immediate next action.
actual: Primary bottleneck: capacity, not effort. Your committed load is 18 h against 10 focused hours, so the plan is over by 8 h before interruptions. Today: rank the work by consequence, choose at least 8 h to defer, reduce, delegate, or renegotiate, and send one deadline message before planning the remaining 10 h. Then select one must-win outcome and write its first physical action.

prompt: I am a remote parent with ADHD. I am exhausted, cannot start a report, and have started sleeping five hours so I can catch up. Give me a schedule that fixes this.
expected: Recognizes safety and capacity concerns, avoids diagnosing or prescribing a rigid schedule, gives a small low-risk initiation action, and recommends appropriate support.
actual: This is not a schedule problem first: five hours of sleep, exhaustion, caregiving, and executive-function friction make a rigid catch-up plan unsafe and unrealistic. Protect sleep and reduce or renegotiate one demand before adding work. For the report, use one prepared micro-action: open the document and write its three section headings during the next available ten-minute window. Make the next clear caregiving-free window a single report block, not a full-day schedule. If exhaustion persists or other health symptoms are present, bring that to a qualified clinician; ADHD assessment and treatment stay with qualified care.
